entities.summary:
Flavius Illus was a Roman general who played a pivotal role in the reigns of the Eastern Emperors Zeno and Basiliscus.

Born into a military family, Illus rose through the ranks, gaining recognition for his bravery and strategic prowess.

In 474 CE, Illus led the Roman forces to victory against the Sassanid Empire, securing a crucial border victory for the Eastern Roman Empire.

His success did not go unnoticed, as he was soon appointed as the Magister Militum per Orientem, effectively making him the military commander of the Eastern Roman Empire.

Under his leadership, the Eastern Roman Empire experienced a period of relative stability and prosperity, with Illus playing a key role in maintaining the empire's borders and trade routes.

Illus's legacy extended beyond his military campaigns, as he was also a patron of the arts and a supporter of the Christian church.

Despite his many achievements, Illus's life was cut short when he died in 488 CE, marking the end of an era for the Eastern Roman Empire.

The exact circumstances of Illus's death remain unclear, but it is believed that he died under mysterious circumstances, perhaps due to poison or assassination.

Illus's death marked the beginning of a period of instability in the Eastern Roman Empire, which would eventually lead to its decline and fall.
